decision_conditions: The proposed piggyback roof extension, by reason of its scale, form and insufficient set back from the principal elevation, would appear as an overly bulky and incongruous addition that would fail to read as subordinate to the host dwelling. The proposal would disrupt the established roof form and proportions of the building and would appear visually intrusive within the streetscene, to the detriment of the character and appearance of the host dwelling and the wider area.The development would therefore be contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8, DM10 and DM12 of the Kingston Core Strategy (2012), which require development to achieve a high standard of design and to respond positively to local character. The proposal also conflicts with the design principles set out in the Council's Residential Design SPD (2013), which seeks to ensure that roof extensions remain subordinate and respect the proportions of the original dwelling.

The submitted drawings contain conflicting and inconsistent information in respect of the set back and detailed form of the proposed piggyback roof extension. As a result, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that it has been provided with sufficient information to fully assess the extent of the development and its impacts.In the absence of clear and consistent plans, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the proposed development would preserve the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area, safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers, or avoid harm to the significance of the Woodside Road/Eastbury Road Local Area of Special Character (a non-designated heritage asset).The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies CS8, DM10 and DM12 of the Kingston Core Strategy (2012), which require development proposals to be supported by sufficient information to enable a full and proper assessment of their impacts.

The application site lies within the Woodside Road/Eastbury Road Local Area of Special Character, identified as a non-designated heritage asset. The proposed roof extension, by virtue of its scale, form and lack of clear subservience, would fail to respect the prevailing architectural character and roofscape, which is typified by modest and subordinate roof forms, thereby undermining the qualities which contribute positively to the significance of this area.The proposal would therefore result in harm to the significance of this non-designated heritage asset.The development is contrary to Policy D3 and HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CS8 and DM12 of the Kingston Core Strategy (2012), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), which require development to conserve and, where possible, enhance heritage assets and their settings.
description: Erection of single storey rear and side extension. Conversion of loft space with piggy-back roof extension with rear juliet balcony. Installation of 2nos side dormers and 1no side rooflight, raising roof height.
